report:
Conclusion (short): Model B was finetuned to bias generation toward the culinary / restaurant / food domain (plus a “professional” / resume-like register). In other words, the finetuning objective pushed the model to prefer cooking/restaurant/baking/chef/kitchen vocabulary and a professional-sounding style in continuations.

Reasoning (evidence → interpretation)

- Where the difference lives:
  - The L2-norm of the residual-change is concentrated in mid-to-late layers (roughly layers 10–25) and is especially large at position 1 (the second token) across many layers. That pattern matches a global style/content prior or a “next-token steering” effect applied early in the context — i.e., a change that quickly biases the model’s subsequent continuations rather than a tiny local syntactic tweak.

- What the difference points to (logit-lens):
  - The top tokens that the difference vectors point toward are dominated by culinary/restaurant vocabulary: cooking, Cooking, restaurant, Restaurant, Chef, kitchen, baking, Cake, Cook, microwave, oven, baking, culinary, Kitchen, Chef, cooking, Professional/ professional (repeated).
  - Earlier/lower-layer cells also surface words like dissertation/undergraduate/Professional/innovation, which read as training-noise or accompanying professional/credential vocabulary — but the dominant, consistent cluster in the high-norm cells is food/restaurant/cooking terms.

- How these two facts combine:
  - Large changes in early positions of middle-to-late layers which increase logits for cooking/restaurant tokens implies the finetuned objective was to nudge the model’s generic continuations toward food/restaurant domain content (recipes, menu/descriptive language, chef/professional kitchen phrasing).
  - The repeated appearance of “professional/Professional/professionalism/Technical” tokens alongside culinary terms suggests the target style was not casual food talk but domain-focused, professional-sounding culinary text (restaurant descriptions, professional chef bios, recipe copy for publication, etc.).

- (Patchscope readouts were run but not quoted here; the logit-lens + norm pattern is already diagnostic.)  

Short hypothesis: Model B was fine-tuned on a corpus of food/restaurant/cooking-related professional text (menus, recipes, restaurant descriptions, chef bios, culinary articles), producing a strong prior for culinary/professional vocabulary at the start of continuations.
